Shared exponential kernel calculations

Source: vignettes/articles/shared-kernel.Rmd
shared-kernel.Rmd

Purpose and availability

The GitHub development version 1.0.1.9000 exports exp_kernel_spec(), as_exp_kernel() and exp_kernel_replay(). These experimental functions provide a shared calculation boundary inside emhawkes. The separate frpp package uses it for its numeric state likelihood. The dependency is frpp -> emhawkes.

The API supplies kernel states and integrals. The calling model owns its baseline, initialization policy, residual distribution, likelihood and random draws. Existing Hawkes event loops and emhawkes.engine selection are unchanged. Publication on GitHub does not update an already installed CRAN version.

Specification and mapping

Numeric alpha and beta are D by K matrices; eta is optional with the same shape. Beta must be positive and equal within each row. Rows are event types and columns are kernels. type_col_map[[i]] selects the columns updated by type i; entries can overlap across event types. Signed components and jumps are retained. These shape rules alone do not guarantee a valid simulator or stationarity. Function-valued kernel parameters and impact callbacks are outside this first interface; conversion rejects them without executing them.

h <- new("hspec", mu = c(.3, .4),
  alpha = matrix(c(.04, .03, .02, .05, .01, .02, .03, .01), 2, 4),
  beta = matrix(rep(c(1.2, 1.7), 4), 2),
  type_col_map = list(c(3L, 1L), c(2L, 4L)))
kernel <- as_exp_kernel(h)

as_exp_kernel() reads kernel slots only. Baselines, mark generators, mark densities and residual laws are not copied or evaluated. The specification contains no evolving state, so replaying it twice does not accumulate events.

Replay contract

Supply observed intervals, types, optional marks and explicit initial components. The first row is the initial state: its interval is zero and it causes no event update. Subsequent zero intervals update events in input order. Replay adds no terminal observation interval and consumes no random numbers.

dt <- c(0, .2, .4, 0, .3)
type <- c(0, 1, 2, 1, 2)
initial <- matrix(.05, 2, 4)
x <- exp_kernel_replay(kernel, dt, type, lambda_component0 = initial)
x$kernel_integral
#>            [,1]       [,2]
#> [1,] 0.00000000 0.00000000
#> [2,] 0.03556202 0.03390937
#> [3,] 0.06586329 0.05582602
#> [4,] 0.00000000 0.00000000
#> [5,] 0.05751446 0.04875125
x$kernel_before
#>           [,1]       [,2]
#> [1,] 0.2000000 0.20000000
#> [2,] 0.1573256 0.14235406
#> [3,] 0.1282896 0.09744984
#> [4,] 0.1782896 0.15744984
#> [5,] 0.1592723 0.12457271
x$final_component
#>            [,1]       [,2]       [,3]       [,4]
#> [1,] 0.06215525 0.05093330 0.02827364 0.06791007
#> [2,] 0.03796829 0.09085156 0.02892112 0.02683174

For M input rows, the ordinary output is:

Output Shape Meaning
kernel_integral M by D Kernel-only integral over each interval; initial row is zero
kernel_before M by D Pre-event component sums; initial row is the initial row sums
final_component D by K State after the final event, or unchanged initial state for M = 1

A scalar initial value expands over all components. A matrix must match D by K; a matching vector follows R’s column-major matrix order. Automatic mean/zero policies and count paths belong to the calling model.

With history = TRUE, component_before and component_after are additionally returned as M by (D times K). Within each row, components are flattened row by row. Histories are allocated only when requested. Ordinary output still stores M by D interval integrals and sums; it is not constant-memory streaming.

full <- exp_kernel_replay(kernel, dt, type, lambda_component0 = initial,
  history = TRUE)
stopifnot(identical(x, full[names(x)]))

Using the result in another model

For a numeric baseline mu, the caller forms pre-event drivers and integrated drivers as follows:

mu <- as.vector(h@mu)
driver_before <- sweep(x$kernel_before, 2, mu, "+")
integrated_driver <- x$kernel_integral + outer(dt, mu)
driver_before
#>           [,1]      [,2]
#> [1,] 0.5000000 0.6000000
#> [2,] 0.4573256 0.5423541
#> [3,] 0.4282896 0.4974498
#> [4,] 0.4782896 0.5574498
#> [5,] 0.4592723 0.5245727
integrated_driver
#>            [,1]      [,2]
#> [1,] 0.00000000 0.0000000
#> [2,] 0.09556202 0.1139094
#> [3,] 0.18586329 0.2158260
#> [4,] 0.00000000 0.0000000
#> [5,] 0.14751446 0.1687513

FRPP combines these with residual density and survival terms. A non-exponential residual law changes the conditional hazard: the kernel driver by itself is not automatically the FRPP conditional intensity. Hawkes-specific stationary means, gradients and Hessian adjustments are not supplied by this API.

Use the exported functions rather than emhawkes:::. The implementation is an R reference path, independent of the likelihood engine option. Internal advance/update helpers and C++ implementation details are not part of this public contract. Event-wise calculations below support independent FRPP event generation; callback kernels remain outside this numeric interface.

Event-wise calculations

exp_kernel_wait() inverts supplied integrated-driver targets using a numeric baseline and current kernel components. It draws no residuals and selects no event. exp_kernel_step() advances the components and optionally applies one mapped event; it also returns component integrals unless integrate = FALSE. Neither function replays a growing path prefix.

component <- initial
candidates <- exp_kernel_wait(kernel, component, mu, residual = c(.7, .9))
event <- which.min(candidates)
next_state <- exp_kernel_step(kernel, component, min(candidates), type = event)
next_state$before
#>             [,1]        [,2]        [,3]        [,4]
#> [1,] 0.005503118 0.005503118 0.005503118 0.005503118
#> [2,] 0.002194278 0.002194278 0.002194278 0.002194278
next_state$after
#>            [,1]        [,2]       [,3]        [,4]
#> [1,] 0.04550312 0.005503118 0.01550312 0.005503118
#> [2,] 0.03219428 0.002194278 0.02219428 0.002194278
next_state$integral
#>            [,1]       [,2]       [,3]       [,4]
#> [1,] 0.03708074 0.03708074 0.03708074 0.03708074
#> [2,] 0.02812101 0.02812101 0.02812101 0.02812101

A zero interval still updates the selected event. type = NULL performs only decay and integration. Signed components are retained. Waiting-time inversion requires admissible decreasing row sums; a finite total driver integral can produce an infinite waiting time when its baseline is zero.

For repeated calculations with fixed parameters, prepare a reusable plan:

plan <- exp_kernel_plan(kernel, mu)
stopifnot(identical(candidates, plan$wait(component, c(.7, .9))))
stopifnot(identical(next_state, plan$step(component, min(candidates), event)))

The plan captures a validated kernel and baseline once. Its wait() and step() functions still check the changing components and arguments. Components remain explicit inputs: the plan stores no event state, history or RNG. It is reusable across independent paths; create a new plan when parameters change. Editing the original specification does not change an existing plan. The plan’s function bindings are locked. Older event-wise functions remain available with their existing checked input contracts.

FRPP owns its residual-generation order, earliest-event selection, count paths, output histories and RNG handling. The event-wise API receives explicit targets and contains no model-specific residual law. Legacy Hawkes and FRPP event loops are unchanged. This is an R reference interface, not a speed improvement claim.
